targetText: The world is our sensation: this is the fundamental premise, which is obscured but in no wise altered by the word “element” and by the theories of the “independent series,” “co-ordination,” and “introjection.” The absurdity of this philosophy lies in the fact that it leads to solipsism, to the recognition of the existence of the philosophising individual only.
explanation: Lenin exposes the fatal dead-end of subjective idealism: reducing reality to sensation inevitably leads to solipsism, an unscientific absurdity that no Machian can logically escape.
